notes: LT001 and LT002 independently reviewed the blinded candidate and reached the same conclusion. In the first review, the process was checked sequentially from specification understanding through architecture, transition semantics, candidate properties, and final RTL. The candidate correctly models synchronous reset with highest priority, accepted writes affecting only the addressed word, registered reads returning the pre-edge memory value, disabled-read hold behavior, independent simultaneous ports, and read-first same-address collisions. In the second review, the key temporal and concurrency boundaries were independently stress-checked. For a simultaneous read and write to the same address, non-blocking assignment semantics cause rd_data_reg to sample the old pre-edge memory value while the memory word receives wr_data after the edge, exactly matching the frozen read-first requirement. Simultaneous accesses to different addresses complete independently, and rd_data has no combinational dependence on rd_addr because it is only an alias of the registered rd_data_reg. The synchronous reset loop clears every memory word and rd_data_reg and prevents read/write operations on the reset edge. No substantive process or RTL error was found. Trusted directed simulation and bounded formal verification pass all configured obligations.
